name: Blue Team — Defense & Detection
tagline: Tools defenders run to detect, monitor, and protect their own estate: SIEM, endpoint telemetry, network monitoring, and hostile-HTTP defense.

tools.name: Elastic Stack (ELK)
tools.desc: Reference open-core SIEM: ingests logs via Beats/Elastic Agent into Elasticsearch (Kibana for UI), and runs the detection engine with EQL/ES|QL/Sigma rules, dashboards, and built-in threat hunting.
tools.when: Your first-stop SIEM when you want one cluster for security detections plus powerful full-text log search and can absorb Elasticsearch operations.
tools.install: docker run -d -p 9200:9200 -e discovery.type=single-node docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:9.5.1 (then add Kibana + Elastic Agent per the docs)

tools.name: Wazuh
tools.desc: Open-source XDR/SIEM pairing an Elastic/OpenSearch backend with a unified agent delivering file-integrity monitoring, security configuration assessment, vulnerability detection, active response, and compliance dashboards.
tools.when: When you want SIEM plus endpoint agent in one cohesive open bundle with built-in compliance reporting (PCI-DSS/HIPAA/SOC 2) and less manual Elasticsearch plumbing.

tools.name: Splunk
tools.desc: Commercial SIEM incumbent (Cisco-owned): SPL search over indexed events, mature dashboards/alerts, and the largest third-party integration ecosystem; licensed per GB/day.
tools.when: When budget exists and you need enterprise SIEM tooling, best-in-class search UX, and vendor support — or as the benchmark when evaluating an all-open stack.

tools.name: Graylog
tools.desc: Open-source log management and SIEM on Elasticsearch/OpenSearch storage, with flexible extraction pipelines (streams + pipeline rules) for parsing, routing, GEOIP, and threat-intel enrichment.
tools.when: Log centralization when you want clean server-side pipelines to poll, enrich, and route messages into destinations like Splunk or Elastic — without running agent fleets or Wazuh-style XDR.
tools.install: curl -L -o graylog-repo.deb https://packages.graylog2.org/repo/packages/graylog-7.1-repository_latest.deb && sudo dpkg -i graylog-repo.deb && sudo apt-get install graylog-server

tools.name: Logstash
tools.desc: Data-shaping pipeline (the 'L' in ELK) that pulls logs and metrics, transforms them — parse, enrich, filter, route — and ships them to Elasticsearch or any other output.
tools.when: The standalone parsing/enrichment middle layer when an agent's native handling or a Beats module isn't enough for messy or appliance-shaped log sources.

tools.name: Velociraptor
tools.desc: Open-source DFIR + endpoint-monitoring framework (Rapid7): the Velociraptor Query Language hunts the entire fleet for forensic artifacts, collects live evidence at scale, and the monitoring engine runs Sigma detections against ETW/eBPF events in real time.
tools.when: Endpoint hunting and incident response at scale — triage thousands of hosts, collect volatile evidence, then keep them monitored with live detections.

tools.name: osquery
tools.desc: SQL-powered agent that exposes OS state — processes, sockets, files, users, listeners — as queryable tables; defenders fire fleet-wide queries instantly and schedule packs for continuous inspection, managed via Fleet.
tools.when: Lightweight cross-platform endpoint telemetry when you want to 'SELECT' answers from every host and ship the results to a SIEM; pair with Fleet (fleetdm) for enroll/query management.

tools.name: Sysmon
tools.desc: Windows Sysinternals driver that logs high-fidelity process creation, network connections, and file writes beyond default auditing; pair with the SwiftOnSecurity (or Modular) config for a solid threat-hunting baseline.
tools.when: On every Windows host where you need attacker-action visibility and can ship its event log to your SIEM — no heavy agent required.

tools.name: LimaCharlie
tools.desc: Cloud-native SecOps platform: an EDR sensor streams verbose endpoint telemetry over TLS in real time, and a YAML-based Detection & Response engine runs the full open Sigma ruleset with automated response actions.
tools.when: When you want EDR plus detection-as-code in the cloud without running a SIEM or agent server yourself; the free Community org covers small estates and labs.
tools.install: preinstalled (SaaS) — create a free Community org at limacharlie.io, then run the per-OS sensor installer and enable the Sigma ruleset

tools.name: Suricata
tools.desc: OISF's multi-threaded open-source IDS/IPS engine that inspects traffic with Snort-compatible rules at multi-Gbps speeds and emits structured EVE JSON alerts (plus PCAP) straight into your SIEM.
tools.when: High-throughput signature detection at your network edge or segmentation points; the default pick for a self-managed NIDS with IPS fallback.
tools.install: sudo add-apt-repository ppa:oisf/suricata-stable && sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install suricata && sudo suricata-update

tools.name: Snort 3
tools.desc: Cisco's next-generation open-source NIDS/IPS: Snort 3 adds multi-threading, a Lua-based policy language, and faster pattern matching over the classic 2.x line, tuned via Talos rules.
tools.when: When you prefer Cisco's Talos rules ecosystem, are migrating an existing Snort 2 deployment, or want SnortML-driven engine tuning.
tools.install: sudo apt-get install snort3 (Ubuntu 22.04+; otherwise build from the source tarball on snort.org)

tools.name: Zeek
tools.desc: Passive network-analysis framework (formerly Bro) that logs rich protocol metadata, file hashes, and events across 70+ log types for later forensics instead of blocking in real time.
tools.when: Deep protocol visibility feeding a SIEM or full-packet archive — run it beside Suricata/Snort because it answers 'what happened', while the engine answers 'alert'.
tools.install: docker pull zeek/zeek (or add the zeek.org apt repo: sudo apt-get install zeek)

tools.name: Security Onion
tools.desc: Turnkey NSM distribution that bundles Suricata (detection + full packet capture), Zeek metadata, Elasticsearch/Kibana dashboards, osquery host visibility, and alert/case management into a single install.
tools.when: Fastest way to stand up a complete detection-and-response platform on one box or a small grid when you don't want to assemble the components yourself.
tools.install: Download the ISO from https://securityonion.com, install, then run: sudo so-setup-network (guided wizard)

tools.name: ModSecurity
tools.desc: The OWASP open-source WAF engine (an OWASP Production project) that inspects HTTP traffic and enforces SecRule policies on Apache/nginx; load the OWASP CRS on top for real attack coverage.
tools.when: Inline HTTP-layer defense when you want the battle-tested rule ecosystem and can commit to tuning false positives against your apps.
tools.install: sudo apt-get install libapache2-mod-security2 (Apache; for nginx compile the module with --with-compat --add-dynamic-module=../ModSecurity-nginx)

tools.name: Coraza
tools.desc: OWASP WAF written in Go with near-full ModSecurity compatibility — runs CRS v4 without the legacy C engine as a library or middleware for Caddy, Traefik, APISIX, and API gateways, ideal for detection-as-code.
tools.when: Cloud-native stacks (Go services, containers, Caddy/Traefik/APISIX) where ModSecurity's build model is awkward but you still want CRS protection.
tools.install: xcaddy build --with github.com/corazawaf/coraza-caddy/v2 (then add the coraza_waf block to the Caddyfile)

tools.name: OWASP CRS
tools.desc: The OWASP flagship Core Rule Set — a community-maintained rule layer detecting SQLi, XSS, scanners, and other OWASP Top 10 attacks that runs on both ModSecurity and Coraza engines; a ruleset, not a standalone tool.
tools.when: The rule layer to load onto any WAF engine so a bare install actually detects web attacks; tune via the anomaly-scoring exclusions to cut false positives.
tools.install: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/coreruleset/coreruleset.git (then Include the CRS config in your WAF engine)

tools.name: Cloudflare WAF
tools.desc: Commercial managed edge WAF (SaaS) that filters traffic on Cloudflare's CDN using managed rulesets (including OWASP CRS coverage) plus bot and rate controls — no servers to run.
tools.when: When your apps already sit behind Cloudflare and you want managed rules, DDoS/bot defense, and zero self-hosting in one panel.
tools.install: preinstalled (SaaS) — enable in the dash.cloudflare.com Security panel, pick a managed ruleset, and tune via custom rules
